description: REQ-201's own EARS clause and worked example list `economy/gig`, `economy/ubi`, `cook`, `self/*`, and `report` as slots that MUST remain presented to the model even while below `BOOTSTRAP_RESERVE_USDC` ('presenting only slots that carry no capital risk to the instance's own treasury (e.g. economy/gig, economy/ubi, cook, self/*, report, and any other slot explicitly tagged non-risking)'). But the very next edge case in the SAME requirement makes the opposite the literal, binding default: 'A slot that exists in registry.json with status: "live" but has no explicit risk tag: defaults to being treated as capital-risking (excluded while below threshold, subject to the open-position carve-out above) ... fail-closed by default, never fail-open by omission.' Acceptance criterion (a) for REQ-201 reads: 'the computed catalog/active-slot list contains only slots that are either (a) not tagged capital-risking, (b) tagged alwaysAvailable:true, or (c) tagged capital-risking but currently holding an open position' -- and (a) is ambiguous between 'lacks a risk tag' and 'is explicitly tagged non-risking', which the edge case resolves in favor of the LATTER (untagged = risky). I read the actual, current registry.json on disk: NOT ONE of its 18 slot entries has any 'risk' field today -- including `economy/gig`, `economy/ubi`, `self/spawn`, `self/spawn-child`, `self/issue-dev`, `self/coordinate`, and `yield`, every one of which REQ-201's own prose names or implies should remain visible to a broke instance. Only `report`/`cook` are given the new `alwaysAvailable: true` override anywhere in the spec -- none of the other 'safe' slots named in REQ-201's EARS clause get any equivalent carve-out. As literally specified, a Phase 3 implementation that satisfies every stated acceptance criterion (fail-closed default for untagged slots; alwaysAvailable:true added ONLY to report/cook, per the edge case's own text: 'The slots this increment marks alwaysAvailable: true are exactly report and cook') would EXCLUDE economy/gig, economy/ubi, and every self/* slot from any instance below the $20 reserve -- which is precisely the population of broke instances this entire feature's increment scope exists to serve ('a new bookkeeping-only catalog eligibility gate that hides capital-risking earn slots from a broke instance's tool menu ... ' whose central worked scenario, per REQ-201's own text and the increment's stated purpose in behavioral-spec.md's intro, is a broke instance using economy/gig to TAKE a gig and earn with $0 capital). This is not a hypothetical migration nicety -- it is the literal, currently-true state of the one file (registry.json) the gate reads risk tags from, and nothing in REQ-201/202's acceptance criteria requires Phase 3 to add explicit `risk: safe` (or equivalent non-risking) tags to economy/gig, economy/ubi, or any self/* slot before this gate ships. The requirement is therefore not implementable unambiguously as the sole compliant behavior consistent with its own EARS clause: a literal, criteria-satisfying implementation directly contradicts the requirement's own stated intent and would break the feature's own headline bootstrap scenario for every currently-broke instance the moment this gate lands.

evidence.snippet: "economy/gig": { "track": "A", ... "status": "live", ... } -- no 'risk' or 'alwaysAvailable' field present anywhere in the file for economy/gig, economy/ubi, self/spawn, self/spawn-child, self/issue-dev, self/coordinate, or yield.
